stem: A nurse anticipates a procedure that may generate splashes or sprays of blood or body fluids toward the face. Which PPE approach is appropriate under Standard Precautions?

options.A: A surgical mask alone even when the eyes may be exposed
options.B: Protective eyewear with a mask, or a face shield that protects the eyes, nose, and mouth, plus other task-indicated PPE
options.C: Gloves alone because mucous-membrane protection is unnecessary for splash risk
options.D: Eye protection only when the client specifically requests it

rationale: CDC Standard Precautions direct healthcare personnel to protect the mucous membranes of the eyes, nose, and mouth during procedures likely to generate splashes or sprays. CDC specifies protective eyewear plus a mask, or a face shield, selected according to the anticipated exposure and used with other indicated PPE. B is correct.
educational_objective: Select appropriate face and eye PPE for anticipated blood/body-fluid splash or spray exposure.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices for Safe Healthcare Delivery in All Settings
source_locator: Personal Protective Equipment section — use protective eyewear and a mask, or a face shield, for procedures/activities that could generate splashes or sprays
source_claim_supported: Standard Precautions require protection of eyes, nose, and mouth from anticipated splashes/sprays using protective eyewear plus a mask or a face shield, with task-appropriate PPE selection.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — standard precautions and PPE
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — Standard Precautions PPE

source_original.stem: A nurse anticipates a procedure with potential splash or spray risk of blood or body fluids. Standard precautions require the nurse to wear:

options.A: A surgical mask alone even when blood or body fluid could splash into the nurse's eyes
options.B: Eye or face protection with other indicated PPE when splash or spray exposure is anticipated
options.C: Gloves alone because standard precautions do not require mucous-membrane protection from splashes
options.D: Eye protection only when the client specifically requests additional protective equipment

source_original.rationale: Standard precautions require eye protection (goggles or a face shield) whenever a procedure or activity carries a reasonably anticipated risk of blood or body fluid splash or spray to the face, protecting the mucous membranes of the eyes from potential pathogen exposure, in addition to other appropriate PPE such as gloves and a mask/gown as indicated.
source_original.source_detail: CDC Core Infection Prevention Practices: eye/face mucous-membrane protection for anticipated splashes or sprays; accessed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Made the keyed PPE combination match CDC exactly: protective eyewear plus mask, or a face shield, rather than the looser phrase 'eye or face protection.' Added explicit eye/nose/mouth mucous-membrane protection and retained task-based PPE selection.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current CDC Core Practices; NCSBN 2026 blueprint
audit_findings.currentness: CDC Core Practices and current eye-protection guidance checked 2026-08-17.
audit_findings.claim_audit: CDC directly specifies eyewear+mask or face shield for anticipated splashes/sprays and task-based PPE selection.

distractor_audit.D: PPE selection is exposure-based, not client-request based.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: B is the only complete Standard Precautions answer.
audit_findings.cueing: Options are parallel PPE strategies without explanatory hints.
audit_findings.blueprint: Standard Precautions and PPE map directly to Safety and Infection Prevention and Control.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked CDC Core Practices and Isolation Precautions recommendations; B remains uniquely correct.
